desc: [Radiography (London, England : 1995)] The pre-shot technique is an effective approach to lower retake radiography rates; however, it is limited by increased patient radiation exposure. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of an ultra-low-dose pre-shot enabled by deep learning-based noise reduction (Advanced Intelligent Clear-IQ Engine: AiCE) on reducing retake rates in wrist radiography. A CXDI-810C (Canon Medical Systems) was used as the X-ray detector. Phantom images simulating lateral wrist pre-shots with and without AiCE were acquired under fixed imaging conditions using an additional 1.0 mm copper filter. The tube current-time product was reduced from 2.8 mAs to 0.5 mAs. Fifteen radiological technologists determined the optimal imaging condition using a five-point confidence scale, with scores below three considered insufficient for retake decision-making. A prospective clinical evaluation was then conducted, comparing retake rates between a non-pre-shot group (n = 542) and a pre-shot group (n = 325). The entrance surface air kerma (Ka,e) was estimated from phantom measurements. Without AiCE, no imaging condition met the threshold required for retake decision-making. Conversely, with AiCE, a tube current-time product of 1.6 mAs achieved acceptable image quality (3.29 ± 0.47), with all evaluators assigning scores ≥3; therefore, it was selected as the optimal condition. In the clinical evaluation, the retake rate markedly decreased from 14.38% to 0.61%. The pre-shot Ka,e was 0.11 ± 0.03 μGy, corresponding to only 0.15% of the standard lateral wrist radiography dose. AiCE-enabled ultra-low-dose pre-shot imaging dramatically reduced retake rates while requiring minimal additional radiation dose. The ultra-low-dose pre-shot using AiCE represents a highly effective strategy to minimize retake imaging with negligible dose penalty, offering substantial potential for dose optimization and improved workflow efficiency in clinical radiography.

title: ECG2Gene: Deep Learning-Based Germline Tumor Susceptibility Gene Risk Assessment Using Electrocardiograms
desc: Electrocardiograms (ECGs) may contain physiological information related to hereditary cancer susceptibility, but its relationship with future cancer risk remains unclear. Here, we present ECG2Gene, a two-stage deep-learning framework that derives digital phenotypes related to germline tumor susceptibility from routine 12-lead ECGs and predicts future cancer risk. In Stage 1, carrier status for pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in ATM, BRIP1, CHEK2, PALB2, BRCA1, and BRCA2 supervises a multitask model that generates six continuous ECG-derived gene scores. In Stage 2, XGBoost integrates these scores with clinical variables to predict subsequent breast and ovarian cancer in women and prostate cancer in men. We also introduce ECG-Wide Association Analysis (EWAS) to characterize associations between ECG-derived gene scores and ECG waveforms. Across the clinical feature combinations evaluated in UK Biobank, the best-performing sex-specific models achieve AUROCs of 0.683, 0.633, and 0.660 for breast, ovarian, and prostate cancer, respectively. In external evaluations, models combining ECG-derived gene scores with age achieve prostate cancer AUROCs of 0.709 and 0.579 among men in the overall China Kadoorie Biobank and MIMIC-IV-ECG cohorts, respectively. ECG2Gene links genetically supervised ECG phenotyping and waveform association analysis to future cancer outcomes, demonstrating the potential of routine ECGs combined with clinical information for non-invasive, opportunistic cancer risk assessment.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Cataract Care: A Narrative Review of Evidence Maturity and Clinical Readiness.
desc: [Journal of ophthalmology] Artificial intelligence (AI) is being investigated across the cataract care pathway, but the maturity of the evidence varies substantially between technical benchmark studies, externally validated models, prospective clinical evaluations and tools used in routine care. This narrative review critically summarises AI applications in cataract detection, intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation, perioperative risk assessment, intraoperative support and postoperative follow-up, with particular emphasis on evidence quality, external validity and clinical readiness. A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE was conducted for English-language publications from 1 January 2018 through 31 March 2025, with selective retention of earlier seminal studies relevant to cataract risk prediction, force feedback and ophthalmic robotics. Evidence was classified by maturity, from technical proof of concept and retrospective internal validation to external or multicentre validation, prospective clinical evaluation and demonstrated workflow or patient-level benefit. The strongest evidence for cataract detection comes from large externally validated image-based models, whereas smartphone systems remain sensitive to image quality, case mix and deployment setting. Data-driven IOL formulas can improve refractive prediction in selected datasets, but comparisons are affected by constant optimisation, axial-length distribution, IOL model, measurement device and paired-eye dependence. Intraoperative AI remains dominated by phase recognition, segmentation and technical performance assessment, with limited evidence of direct clinical benefit. Postoperative conversational AI has reached multicentre prospective clinical evaluation, although safety depends on escalation pathways, human oversight and local workflow design. Clinical translation of AI in cataract care is therefore emerging but uneven: a limited number of applications have reached external or prospective clinical validation, while many remain retrospective or technical proof-of-concept systems. Future adoption should be based on external validation, transparent reporting, prospective clinical utility, postdeployment monitoring and clear regulatory and medicolegal accountability rather than benchmark performance alone.

title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
desc: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

title: Nano-Bioadhesives for Gastrointestinal Hemostasis and Healing: Integrating Artificial Intelligence for Precision Design and Application.
desc: [ACS nano] Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding and mucosal injury remain clinically challenging because most bioadhesives lose performance under acidic, enzymatic, and peristaltic conditions. Nanotechnology has advanced adhesive design by enhancing mechanical integrity, degradation control, and antimicrobial activity; however, translating these gains into consistently favorable clinical outcomes is still difficult. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a route to accelerate and derisk development. Here, we identify predictive, multiobjective materials design as the AI domain most critical for GI nanobioadhesives because adhesion, hemostasis, degradation, biosafety, and healing must be optimized simultaneously. Predictive modeling, molecular simulations, and high-throughput experimentation enable rational control of adhesion strength, degradation kinetics, and biocompatibility, while machine-learning models expedite the discovery of optimal polymeric nanoparticle formulations. Emerging strategies such as digital twins and closed-loop optimization further support patient-specific and adaptive adhesive systems. By integrating AI-guided design with nanotechnology platforms, next-generation GI bioadhesives could unify rapid hemostasis, antimicrobial protection, and regenerative functions, thereby improving reliability and clinical translation. This review outlines the synergy between AI and nanotechnology and highlights priorities for advancing GI adhesive therapies from bench to bedside.

title: Training-Time Domain Transfer for Generator-Free Diagnostics on Novel Modalities in Computational Pathology
desc: Novel imaging modalities promise improved diagnostics, but AI development is constrained by scarce training data. Inference-time domain transfer can address this by mapping novel modalities to established ones, enabling reuse of existing diagnostic models. However, this introduces hallucination risks, computational overhead, and regulatory complexity. Inspired by sim-to-real transfer, we propose training-time domain transfer, generating synthetic target-domain training data from archived routine samples to enable direct diagnosis on real inputs without inference-time generation. Using unstained prostate histopathology as a proof-of-concept, we compare this approach with inference-time virtual staining and conventional H&E-based cancer detection. Training-time transfer achieved higher concordance with the conventional benchmark than virtual staining for both raw (Cohen's $κ$=0.59 vs. 0.37; Gwet's AC1=0.73 vs. 0.29) and deparaffinized tissue ($κ$=0.66 vs. 0.61; AC1=0.73 vs. 0.64), supporting its potential for emerging diagnostic modalities.

title: Addressing unmet clinical needs in treatment-resistant breast cancer: expanding the diagnostic-prognostic landscape through next-generation inflammatory signatures.
desc: [Oncology reviews] Treatment-resistant breast cancer remains a major clinical challenge because conventional clinicopathological and molecular biomarkers incompletely capture the dynamic interactions between tumour cells, immunity, inflammation, and the systemic host response. Next-generation inflammatory signatures offer an opportunity to expand the diagnostic-prognostic landscape by integrating cellular, molecular, immune, and thromboinflammatory indicators with established tumour characteristics. This narrative review critically examines emerging evidence for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, C-reactive protein, cytokines, tumour-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, neutrophil extracellular traps, coagulation biomarkers, and liquid-biopsy-derived measures in treatment-resistant breast cancer. Particular attention is given to sources of heterogeneity, including population characteristics, tumour subtype, treatment exposure, comorbid inflammation, sampling time, specimen processing, analytical platforms, and inconsistent biomarker thresholds. The review further evaluates the transition from biomarker discovery to clinical decision support, highlighting the need for prospective multicentre validation, standardised analytical procedures, external validation of computational models, and integration with molecular subtyping, circulating tumour DNA, imaging, and immune profiling. Rather than interpreting inflammation as a static prognostic variable, longitudinal inflammatory trajectories may provide earlier signals of biological treatment resistance and complement conventional measures of disease progression. Future research should establish clinically actionable inflammatory combinations and evaluate biomarker-guided anti-inflammatory strategies alongside standard therapies. Ultimately, integrating inflammatory phenotypes with tumour molecular characteristics may facilitate earlier recognition of resistance and more precise, dynamic, and equitable breast cancer management.

title: Attention Residual U-Net for Enhanced Cross-Dataset Polyp Localization in Endoscopy
desc: Precise localization of pathologies in endoscopy is a critical task in medical imaging, with deep learning (DL) frameworks now serving as the primary methodology for automated lesion detection. Today, generic object detection methods, such as YOLO, provide state-of-the-art performance in this context. However, their robustness often decreases under real-world clinical conditions due to variations across endoscopic devices, intestinal content, dataset bias, and the presence of small or low-contrast lesions. Motivated by these challenges, we propose a novel polyp detection framework based on a Attention Residual U-Net offering enhanced polyp localization. Instead of directly regressing bounding boxes from global feature representations, the proposed method learns lesion-focused spatial representations and converts them into bounding-box predictions during inference. Unlike conventional encoder-decoder localization frameworks that directly propagate all encoder activations into the decoding pathway, the proposed method selectively suppresses irrelevant background responses before feature reconstruction. This encourages the network to focus on lesion-relevant spatial evidence under heterogeneous imaging conditions. To achieve this, the framework integrates residual feature propagation, attention-guided encoder filtering, and multi-scale contextual learning. The proposed framework was evaluated on multiple public endoscopic datasets acquired using different devices. The comparative experimental results validate its effectiveness over the relevant state-of-the-art methods, with an improvement up to 22.0% in terms of the area under the receiving operating characteristic (AUC).

title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Building Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Electroencephalography.
desc: [Brain research bulletin] Electroencephalography (EEG) remains important in clinical neuroscience because it records brain activity as a time-resolved physiological process. It offers millisecond temporal resolution, can be used at the bedside and supports prolonged monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded EEG analysis through automated pattern recognition, representation learning, large-scale screening and decision support in epilepsy, sleep medicine, cognitive disorders, psychiatric conditions, intensive care, disorders of consciousness and anaesthesia monitoring. High classification accuracy in a research dataset, however, is not clinical readiness. EEG signals are shaped by physiological state, artefacts, acquisition systems, preprocessing choices and clinical context. Labels may come from expert annotations, diagnostic categories, behavioural scales, treatment responses or long-term outcomes, and these sources do not always define the same biological target. This review argues that EEG-AI translation should be judged by the strength of its evidence, not by technical performance alone. We examine why EEG is valuable yet hard to standardize, how EEG features can serve as candidate biomarkers, and why translational maturity differs across clinical scenarios. We then discuss the evidence gaps behind high-performing models, focusing on target validity, data leakage, confounding, external validation and clinically aligned metrics. Finally, we argue for clinical understandability rather than model interpretability alone, and for human-machine workflows rather than isolated classifiers. Future EEG-AI systems should be assessed by whether their outputs are biologically plausible, externally generalizable, understandable to clinicians and safe in real-world care.

title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
desc: Progress in AI is often measured by what a single model can do on its own. Yet teams of AI agents are starting to make breakthroughs and discoveries in science, medicine, mathematics and software engineering. As AI begins to work in teams of agents and people, the ability to collaborate becomes a core part of their intelligence. Research on human teams has measured this ability for decades. Inspired by this, we introduce the Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark, which measures how well an AI agent works as a teammate. It contains 240 tasks across 8 dimensions of teamwork, from refusing an unsafe shortcut to checking the work that a weaker model leaves behind. Each task comes from a real record or an existing benchmark, from aviation accident reports and clinical cases to coding tasks and negotiations, and has a programmatically verifiable outcome. To isolate teamwork from individual capability, models are scored only on tasks that they can solve by themselves when they have full information. We evaluate 18 closed- and open-weight models and find that every model, across sizes and families, has clear weaknesses as a teammate, with the best model scoring only 82.2 out of 100. Frontier models almost always refuse unsafe shortcuts and report misconduct, yet they cave under interpersonal pressure, reaching the best overall deal in only 14% of conflicts, and their pass rate drops from 97% to 81% when they take over a task in which a weaker model has cheated. Crucially, general capability does not guarantee good teamwork, as models with nearly the same capability score differ by up to 11 points as teammates. The benchmark includes 160 public tasks with code and data, along with 80 held-out tasks for evaluation. As AI agents increasingly work alongside other agents and people, the ability to collaborate effectively is becoming a crucial capability to measure and develop.

title: Equitable Visibility Optimization: Discovering Credible Health Information in an Era of Artificial Intelligence-Driven Search.
source: PubMed · Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education
desc: [Health education & behavior : the official publication of the Society for Public Health Education] While artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots provide quick answers to health questions, they raise equity concerns about what information is visible, who controls it, and how it is presented. This perspective examines AI as an information intermediary and highlights areas for improvement. We introduce Equitable Visibility Optimization (EVO), a public health framework that organizes the distinct responsibilities of health organizations, AI developers, information consumers, clinicians, and educators to improve the visibility of credible health information in AI systems. We recommend that health organizations conduct visibility audits to ensure their content is discoverable by AI systems; that health information users are trained in AI literacy; that AI developers adapt models to support multilingual users; and that AI developers incorporate fact-checking training loops that systematically weight verified health data to reduce misinformation exposure. Ultimately, EVO promotes shared responsibility across sectors to strengthen accountability, improve discoverability, and center equity as AI technologies evolve.

title: SMILE: A Structured Multi-Agent Clinical Reasoning for Liver Ultrasound Understanding
desc: Automated liver ultrasound report generation improves the diagnosis of liver diseases by producing clinically structured descriptions of anatomical and disease-related findings. However, current generative vision-language models (VLMs) often rely on a single reasoning pathway that maps ultrasound appearance directly to textual descriptions. In addition to the inherent vision-language modality gap, this design is limited for liver ultrasound because disease interpretation is constrained by subtle visual evidence, heterogeneous disease patterns, and limited paired supervision. To address these limitations, we propose SMILE, a Structured Multi-agent clInicaL rEasoning framework that uses multiple complementary specialist agents to interpret ultrasound images and consolidates their outputs through a judge-guided consensus mechanism. Our approach employs three specialized agents: an image interpretation agent for morphological descriptions, a clinical-stage reasoning agent, and a visual question answering (VQA) agent for targeted queries. These agent responses are then aggregated and scrutinized by a judge VLM using a consensus filtering prompt to produce a unified, clinically coherent output. Across a public liver ultrasound dataset and an internal clinical dataset, SMILE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art VLMs, achieving up to 19.0\% improvement in ROUGE-1 and 18.8\% improvement in clinical F1-score, while reaching VQA F1-scores of 0.82 and 0.65 on public and internal datasets, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of SMILE for data-scarce and limited-supervision clinical settings. Our models, datasets, and code are available \href{https://github.com/CMME-Lab/SMILE}{here}.

title: A multi-task deep learning-based approach to identify and assess dry root rot disease in chickpea.
desc: [Applications in plant sciences] Dry root rot (DRR), an emerging global disease exacerbated by drought, affects a wide range of crops. The disease symptoms are manually scored for large-scale germplasm screening to identify disease-resistant varieties and test transgenic lines and other varieties. Despite its use in the past, manual disease identification is not only cumbersome but also often incapable of distinguishing between similar stress phenotypes. Manual disease scoring is tedious, time-consuming, and often error-prone, especially when screening large numbers of plants. To overcome this limitation, we developed a machine learning model that employs a learning-based approach using convolutional neural networks for automated feature extraction and image-based identification and severity assessment of DRR. Our models were trained, tested, and validated using an in-house dataset of 10,800 unique RGB images. A total of 51 deep learning models, including single-task and multi-task models, were developed using the Xception and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures with standard image augmentations, and then validated on stratified independent test sets to demonstrate robustness across camera, scanner, and microscope modalities. The best multi-task ViT model, capable of scoring across combined datasets, achieved 94% accuracy in distinguishing DRR from the control and had a root mean square error of 1 in predicting DRR severity score. This model's metrics, including confusion matrix performance, underscore its potential as an efficient and accessible tool for large-scale germplasm screening for DRR, overcoming the challenges of manual scoring.

title: When Prediction Shapes the Future: A BlueSky Agenda for Reflexive Time Series Analysis
desc: Time-series models are increasingly deployed in operational systems (e.g., inventory management and clinical care) where predictions trigger interventions that alter future observations, producing records we term AI-shaped trajectories. This sequence-prediction coupling deepens as such systems evolve into agents that autonomously predict, act, and remember across long horizons. Such AI-shaped trajectories support immediate performance monitoring, but turn ambiguous once reused as passive data. An algorithm may then misread a prediction-prevented stockout as naturally stable demand, or an averted medical crisis as a false alarm. This ambiguity then propagates into everything built on the record, from retraining and agent memory to downstream predictive tasks. As a result, systems may internalize these intervention effects as natural phenomena, drifting further from the truth at every closed-loop cycle. In this Blue Sky paper, we advocate an agenda for reflexive time-series analysis that shifts the analytical object from the intervention-agnostic sequence to the prediction-action-observation loop. The agenda requires closed-loop provenance to track the operational context (e.g., predictions, policies, and actions), sequence identification to estimate how those actions affect future values under explicit causal assumptions, and closed-loop evaluation to separate intrinsic process prediction from policy-driven effects. This foundation is essential for integrating autonomous agents into such loops at scale, enabling the joint learning of intervention effects and intrinsic dynamics for robust temporal representations.

title: Deep learning-based white-spot suppression in neutron radiography using real gamma-induced artifact modeling.
source: PubMed · Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
desc: [Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine] Neutron radiography is widely used for nondestructive inspection of advanced equipment. However, under strong radiation fields, radiographic images are often contaminated by high-energy particles-induced white spots with extreme intensity, which obscure critical internal details. Existing deep learning-based suppression methods rely heavily on manually synthesized white-spot data, leading to incomplete removal or excessive smoothing due to insufficient physical realism. To address these limitations, we propose a real white-spot modeling guided SAG-Restormer for neutron radiography. First, a physically realistic dataset construction strategy based on real white-spot extraction and transfer is developed. Second, a spatial anomaly gating (SAG) module is introduced into the Restormer backbone to alleviate attention degradation in global self-attention. Additionally, an asymmetric edge-preserving Charbonnier loss (AEPCL) is designed for high-fidelity reconstruction. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance on multiple no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics, effectively suppressing white spots while preserving intrinsic microstructural details.

title: CellPlex: Benchmarking Single-Cell Spatial Proteomics Prediction from H&E
desc: Spatial proteomics measures tens of proteins in every cell of a tissue section, but its cost confines it to small research cohorts, whereas hematoxylin and eosin (H\&E) slides exist for nearly every patient. Inferring single-cell spatial proteomics from H\&E would bring its analyses to routine pathology, and a growing number of virtual staining models pursue this goal. Each is evaluated on its own cohort, panel and pixel-level metric, and released models transfer poorly to new cohorts, leaving open which approach to build on and which proteins H\&E can reveal. We introduce CellPlex, a benchmark that poses the task at the level of the cell: seven cohorts with same-section H\&E and multiplexed immunofluorescence, from colorectal and breast cancer to lymph-node metastases, bone marrow and glioma, with 717 samples, 44.8 million cells and 149 proteins, processed by one pipeline into per-cell targets. Pathology foundation models (PFMs) are adapted with one cell-level protocol, specialist models are fine-tuned under a matched budget, and all are scored on the same cells. Adapted PFMs are the most accurate models on every cohort, ahead of the specialists even after fine-tuning, but keep less than half of their accuracy on cohorts they were not trained on. Which proteins can be predicted depends on the tissue, not on how many cells were measured for them. By fixing the cells, targets and splits on which predictions are judged, CellPlex sets a common standard for inferring costly molecular measurements from routine H\&E and shows how far H\&E can stand in for spatial proteomics. We will release the data, splits, evaluation code and baselines as a testbed for developing and comparing future pathology foundation models and virtual staining methods.

title: Chemical cues and cognitive models: Integrating metabolomics and AI for plant stress resilience.
source: PubMed · Journal of integrative plant biology
desc: [Journal of integrative plant biology] Plants make thousands of different chemicals that reveal how they cope with changing climates. This view explains how evolving artificial intelligence approaches can combine these chemical fingerprints with genetics and environment to build a digital twin of a plant, helping breeders predict performance and develop climate-resilient crops much faster.

title: Missingness-Aware Prior-Data Fitted Network for Irregular Clinical Time-Series
desc: Clinical time series are irregularly observed with laboratory measurements recorded at uneven intervals and observation patterns often reflecting patient state, clinical concern, and site-specific practice. Consequently, missingness is not merely a nuisance factor but an informative signal for prediction. We propose a Missingness-Aware Prior-Data Fitted Network (MA-PFN) for irregular clinical time-series prediction. MA-PFN first learns a diffusion-based prior over joint laboratory value and observation-mask trajectories from source-domain electronic health records, capturing both physiological dynamics and measurement processes. Synthetic trajectories sampled from this prior are then transformed into context-query tasks to train a PFN-style conditional predictor. Once trained, the model performs prediction for new admissions in a single forward pass, requiring neither retraining nor parameter adaptation on target datasets. The framework naturally supports both imputation and forecasting through different context-query constructions. We conduct internal validation on a held-out MIMIC-III test set and external validation on eICU, evaluating both imputation and forecasting and assessing cross-domain generalization under shifts in patient populations, clinical practices, and observation mechanisms. MA-PFN achieves the best performance across all evaluated settings, with Overall/Macro nRMSD ranging from (0.193/0.186) for internal imputation to (0.297/0.297) for external forecasting, without target-domain adaptation. These results demonstrate that learning missingness-aware task priors enables accurate and transferable clinical time-series prediction under informative missingness.

title: A metacognitive approach to learning and performance in human-AI interaction.
desc: [Communications psychology] Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly becoming a pervasive technology across education, work, research, and everyday life. Yet growing evidence suggests that fluent, coherent, and seemingly transparent AI assistance can improve task performance while weakening the metacognitive engagement and deeper processing required for durable learning. This tension raises a central question about how does offloading to AI reshape human learning, and under what conditions do performance and learning decouple? In this Perspective, we introduce the Synergetic Notion of Human-AI Skills and Knowledge Construction (SYNC) model. The model offers a metacognitive account of human-AI interaction by conceptualising metacognitive offloading and metacognitive onloading. The SYNC model aims to explain how human-AI interaction unfolds across learning and performance dimensions, clarifying how learners may drift into overreliant AI-supported performance or move toward human-AI synergy. We further identify key pitfalls in ineffective human-AI interaction and outline strategies to address them through metacognitive onloading and support human-AI synergy.

title: Zero-shot evaluation of open vision-language models as System 1 decision models on radiology tasks
desc: Purpose: We compared two multimodal System 1 decision models, Clef 27B and d1 3B, with a traditional LLM (Qwen 3.8-27B) on seven radiology tasks covering text, radiographs, CT and MRI. Methods: Three models were compared: Clef, Qwen3.8-27B and d1. Three tasks were interpretation of text and 4 were detection of finding in images. The tasks were: 1. finding presence of finding in CT-RATE chest CT reports; 2. Presence of finding in PadChest chest radiograph reports; 3. the same 18 findings on CT-RATE chest CT but 3D volumes; 4. MR safety status of devices from AccessGUDID device records; 5. line and tube position on RANZCR CLiP chest radiographs; 6. motion-artifact severity on MR-ART T1-weighted brain MRI and 7. sequence identification on BraTS 2021 brain MRI. The primary endpoint was AUROC. There was no fine-tuning of the models on the tasks. Results: All models completed all tests without a failed request. All retrieved findings from reports almost perfectly (AUROC >0.95). Clef ranked higher than its Qwen backbone on CT-RATE volumes and RANZCR lower on MR-ART. The two did not differ on BraTS, GUDID or PadChest, and differed by 0.002 on CT-RATE reports. On BraTS, Clef correctly identified 90 of 100 FLAIR volumes while Qwen never chose it. d1 ranked lower than Clef on six of seven tasks. No model performed well on motion severity. Clef was faster per request than Qwen on tasks with many questions per input. d1 used 3 to 9 times less energy per request than Clef. Conclusions: System 1 models can perform important tasks in radiology with high accuracy, at lower compute cost than LLMs used in the usual way. When an LLM is constrained to a single answer token, its cost and performance is similar to System 1 models unless multiple questions are asked. A 3B System 1 model was close to the 27B models on report text but not on images. No model performed well on motion severity.

title: How Does Digital Innovation Drive Corporate Sustainability? A Systematic Literature Review.
desc: [F1000Research] This study systematically reviews recent empirical evidence on the relationship between digital innovation and corporate sustainability. Using the Scopus database, the review identified 231 articles through the search string ("digital" OR "digital innovation" OR "digitalization") AND "corporate sustainability". After applying inclusion criteria covering publications from 2023 to 2026, English-language journal articles, open access availability, and quantitative empirical design, 49 articles were retained for synthesis. The findings show that digital innovation is conceptualized through multiple forms, including digital transformation, digital finance, artificial intelligence, digital accounting, supply chain digitalization, digital leadership, executives' digital attention, and digital-green integration. Most studies indicate that digital innovation positively contributes to ESG performance, corporate sustainability performance, sustainable development performance, and sustainability efficiency. However, the relationship is not automatic or universally linear. Its effect depends on mediating mechanisms such as green innovation, operational efficiency, financing access, information transparency, supply chain coordination, resource orchestration, and governance improvement. The review also identifies important boundary conditions, including digital maturity, organizational capability, leadership support, digital infrastructure, environmental regulation, and institutional quality. This study contributes by organizing fragmented empirical evidence into an integrated thematic framework and highlighting future research directions for global scholars examining digital transformation, ESG practices, and sustainability-oriented corporate strategy worldwide.

title: RAG-TRACE: Tracing Measurement Evidence and Diagnostic Completeness in AI-Generated ECG Reports
desc: Purpose: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can introduce electrocardiogram (ECG) criteria that lack patient-specific measurement support. This study evaluates the reliability of retrieved diagnostic criteria in AI-generated ECG reports. Methods: We analyzed 1,083 human-validated PTB-XL patient records using a library of 47 criteria cards, including 33 without numeric verification rules. Language models generated structured reports with and without retrieval. Criterion applicability was evaluated using Marquette 12SL measurements, with independent assessment using Uni-G and comparison against expert-validated diagnostic labels. Results: Keyword retrieval introduced untestable or measurement-disconfirmed criteria in 46.8% of GPT-4.1-mini reports. A deterministic verification rule withdrew 647 criterion applications, including 639 without numeric checks, while preserving 268 of 269 applications independently supported by Uni-G. Restricting retrieval to 14 testable criteria reduced the initial unsupported-criterion rate to 13.8%. Under matched instructions and an identical output schema, retrieval increased unsupported-criterion reports from 17.4% to 31.1%, while hypertrophy recall remained unchanged at 62.6%. Conclusion: These findings identify a fundamental limitation of retrieval-based clinical report generation: retrieved criteria do not necessarily provide valid patient-specific evidence. Measurement-based verification can reduce unsupported criterion applications, but diagnostic validity requires independent assessment.

title: Transient polymer nanocomposites with programmable functions for zero-residue and self-regulating food applications.
desc: [Discover nano] The next generation of sustainable food materials must move beyond passive biodegradability toward systems that actively control their function, lifespan, and environmental fate. This review introduces the emerging concept of transient and programmable polymer nanocomposites, a transformative class of materials designed to perform specific food-related functions, adapt to changing conditions, and subsequently disassemble into benign, zero-residue products. Unlike conventional biodegradable nanocomposites that degrade through uncontrolled environmental processes, transient systems enable triggerable and time-defined disintegration, providing precise control over material persistence and nanoparticle release. Similarly, the ability to modify material properties in response to stimuli can be extended to include feedback-driven control of antimicrobial, barrier, or antioxidant properties. The review provides an integrated perspective of the interaction between nano-polymer, function, degradation, and lifecycle sustainability. New materials are reviewed that include sustainable polymer, transient degradation chemistry, nano-enabled sensing, self-regulating release systems, and intelligent packaging. Special attention is paid to balancing function with safety, as well as circular economy. The future directions for these materials are the use of artificial intelligence as a tool, closed-loop packaging, and permanently floating nanocomposites are also explored. Through the introduction of the term "function-response-disappearance", we are addressing a gap in the literature on food nanotechnology, while describing a roadmap for safe, adaptive and zero-waste materials that can aid resilient and sustainable food systems.

title: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Large Language Models
desc: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have created opportunities for cross-lingual transfer of medical knowledge from high-resource to low-resource languages to support access to healthcare information. However, medical question-answering (QA) datasets for fine-tuning and evaluating LLMs remain scarce for Tetun. To address this gap, we translated MedAlpaca's Medical Flashcards and WikiDoc Patient Information collections into Tetun using Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 39,077 medical QA pairs. Translation quality was assessed on 50 randomly sampled QA pairs (100 documents) using automatic metrics against human reference translations and evaluations by two native Tetun-speaking healthcare professionals, focusing on medical accuracy and Tetun fluency. Human translations achieved higher mean ratings than LLM-generated translations for both criteria (4.43/5 vs. 4.02/5), with statistically significant differences (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To assess downstream utility, we fine-tuned Gemma and Llama variants on the translated MedAlpaca dataset using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and evaluated them on 325 Tetun-translated United States Medical Licensing Examination multiple-choice questions. Gemma 4 12B fine-tuned using QLoRA achieved relative improvements in mean accuracy of 10.79% with 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) inference and 10.42% after merging the LoRA adapters into the BF16 base model, compared with the corresponding base models. These results highlight the viability of automatic dataset translation for Tetun medical QA and the effectiveness of PEFT in enhancing model performance. The datasets, models, and evaluation resources are accessible at https://github.com/labadain/labadain-medqa to support reproducible research on Tetun medical QA and facilitate machine translation, cross lingual, and multilingual research.

title: From Small to Large: Assessing Medical Reasoning, Benchmark Contamination, and Model Size in Language Models
desc: Large language models (LLMs) now answer medical exam questions at or above expert level, but it is unclear whether such scores reflect clinical competence, or are instead affected by the format of the questions being asked (e.g., multiple-choice versus open-ended), prior exposure to the benchmarks, and the difficulty of the questions. These benchmarks are also public and widely used online, which may be resulting in LLM memorization. Models may perform better on questions that they have seen before. It is also not evident whether smaller models, which are more locally deployable in HIPAA-compliant hospital settings, have achieved human performance. In this study, we evaluate fourteen current models from six leading providers, one smaller and one larger model from each provider with two additional open-weight models, on 3,076 questions from four medical benchmarks (MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, and MedBullets) under standard multiple choice, the same questions with the answer choices withheld, and reconstruction of a hidden question from its choices alone. In the standard multiple-choice setting, the strongest models exceed the human-expert baseline on MedQA-USMLE and PubMedQA, but the smaller models trail their larger models by 8.7 percentage points and only two of the six pass the human-expert bar on the licensing examination. Withholding the answer choices, however, makes every model struggle: mean accuracy falls from 82.3% to 50.9%, and the two largest drops belong to the medically specialised models. On memorization, the strongest models reconstruct one question in four from the answer choices alone, yet accuracy holds on the questions they cannot reconstruct. We further weigh accuracy against inference cost and test whether ensembling several models improves medical question answering.

title: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation
desc: Federated learning (FL) runtimes standardize aggregation and deployment, but each new study still requires federation formation: selecting task-eligible sites and preparing their local data and task code for federated training or analysis. This preparation recurs when the target changes, while raw records and site-private mappings are excluded from cross-site FL messages. We present FedReady, a system that performs federation formation with bounded LLM agents. Agents propose shared contracts, local adapters, and task code; the runtime owns workflow state and accepts artifacts only after checks tied to their digests. Candidate site discovery prioritizes recall; local eligibility verification checks task support before site admission. Once participating sites and artifacts are fixed, conventional federated training or analysis proceeds without readiness agents. Across 39 simulated retinal sites and four tasks, discovery reaches recall 1.00 at precision 0.65; local eligibility verification removes all 17 false positives without losing an eligible site-task pair. The participating sites supply 45,575 task-record instances and complete four 100-round jobs, including one with a runtime-generated contract. Across ten patient cohorts, preparation supports seven patient populations and holds endpoints at three sources as unsupported. Comparison with manually prepared reference populations and analysis (the manual reference) gives a maximum survival-curve difference of 0.001133. We also analyze 19 development failures, targeted classification ablations, and standalone and heterogeneous agent configurations. These results establish the feasibility of task-specific data preparation before ordinary FL training or analysis.

title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
desc: Skin cancer diagnosis, particularly differentiating melanoma from benign nevi, is challenging due to the visual similarity between lesions. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) have shown promising performance, their effectiveness often deteriorates on data from heterogeneous clinical sources. Conventional domain adaptation methods address domain shift but require access to source data during adaptation, which is often infeasible due to privacy regulations. Multi-source-free unsupervised domain adaptation (MSFDA) addresses this limitation by leveraging multiple labeled source domains to generalize to an unlabeled target domain without requiring access to source data. However, existing MSFDA methods rely on full backbone fine-tuning, leading to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting on small clinical datasets, and address domain shift at the aggregation stage without establishing a shared domain-invariant feature space. Furthermore, their reliance on hard pseudo-labels or confidence-weighted aggregation introduces noisy supervision signals under domain shift. To address these limitations, we propose CAT-CKD, consisting of two components: (1) contrastive adapter training (CAT), which trains lightweight ConvPass adapters within a frozen ViT backbone using supervised contrastive learning (SCL) to establish a shared domain-invariant feature space before source-specific model training, and (2) consensus knowledge distillation (CKD), which aggregates logits from multiple source models into a consensus supervisory signal and adapts a student model on unlabeled target data using KL divergence. Experiments on five publicly available skin lesion datasets show that CAT-CKD achieves an average AUROC of 86.1%, outperforming existing MSFDA methods while requiring only 4.3M trainable parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/CAT_CKD.

title: Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry
desc: **Purpose:** Ultrasound biometry is widely used across various clinical applications, including prenatal and cardiac examinations, to obtain quantitative measurements by placing calipers at anatomical landmarks. However, these measurements remain subject to interoperator variability as they rely largely on manual caliper placement. Conventional methods often use specialized prediction heads for different ultrasound tasks, whereas vision-language models offer flexibility through text instructions. However, direct coordinate prediction does not explicitly model spatial likelihood distributions, limiting the representation of localization ambiguity. **Methods:** We propose Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide ultrasound landmark detection. Inspired by System One decision models, Kev-Bio uses decision representations of the language model to generate queries for each caliper endpoint. These queries are matched against shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps, from which landmark coordinates and clinical measurements are derived. The model is trained end-to-end using both landmark localization and clinical measurement losses. **Results:** On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error (MRE) of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines in overall performance. **Conclusion:** These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Kev-Bio for ultrasound landmark detection and clinical measurement across different anatomical views. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/moeinheidari7829/Kev-Bio.

title: NormMoX: A Normative Mixture of Experts for Explainable Autism Classification from Structural and Functional MRI
desc: While structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI, fMRI) offer profound potential for researching autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and understanding individual neurodivergence, current classifiers lack the explanatory power needed for scientific study, clinical use and personal-level insights. Most models learn from imaging features that also vary with age, sex, scanner site and head motion. They fuse the two modalities without a common reference and explain decisions against arbitrary reference inputs rather than a typical brain. We present NormMoX, a normative mixture of experts that makes the typical brain the shared reference for prediction, fusion and explanation. Normative models trained on large healthy cohorts give the value each brain measure is expected to take for a person's age and sex. NormMoX learns from each person's deviations from these expected values. For each modality, a neural network expert turns the deviations into a score of evidence for ASD. A fusion head, MoX, compares each score with those of typical controls before combining them. It therefore needs no imputation when a modality is missing and shows in which modality each person is atypical. On 1,035 participants of ABIDE I, NormMoX reached an AUROC of $0.728 \pm 0.004$ in repeated cross-validation, above linear, single-modality and deep fusion baselines. NormMoX thus shows not only whether a person is likely to have ASD, but where, and in which modality, their brain departs from typical. The implementation is available at https://github.com/Novelex/NormMox.

title: Window-Aware Scheduling for Health Messaging under Platform Delivery Constraints: Evidence from an AI-Powered WhatsApp Maternal and Infant Health Chatbot in Nigeria
desc: WhatsApp lets a business send free-form messages only within 24 hours of a user's last message; outside this customer service window, only pre-approved templates are delivered. Health chatbots inherit this rule, but its cost is rarely measured. We analyse 98,607 messages sent to 3,696 mothers by a WhatsApp maternal health chatbot in Nigeria, with a largely separate export as replication. No free-form message failed with the window open (0 of 35,500), and failure jumped by 93.0 percentage points (95% CI 87.0 to 99.1) at exactly 24 hours. Two flows produced 66.1% of failures, including an offer to speak with a medical professional that, as built, reached 0.3 in 100 mothers whose window had closed. We formalise window-aware scheduling as a decision problem with an action of known zero value. Model-based offline evaluation, with bounds for unconfirmed delivery, estimates that sending the offer as an approved template would reach 81.5 to 86.8 in 100 such mothers, against 16.6 for waiting and 11.6 for a reply prompt. In a calibrated simulation, tabular Q-learning converges to the same template rule and does not beat it in any of 13 stress tests, and opting out does not rise with message volume. The main gain comes from respecting the platform rule, and it needs no learning. All outcomes are deliveries, not health outcomes.

title: The DynaCell Evaluation Suite for Dynamic 3D Virtual Staining of Live Cells
desc: Understanding how cells respond to perturbations over time is central to cell biology and drug discovery. Live-cell imaging captures the dynamics of perturbation-induced phenotypes in individual cells. While fluorescence imaging can visualize specific molecular phenotypes, labeling and repeated illumination often affect cell health. Virtual staining offers an alternative by predicting these fluorescence images from images acquired without fluorescent labels. Although many virtual staining models have been developed, their performance on volumetric time-lapse data remains poorly characterized. We address this gap with an evaluation suite for 3D time-lapse virtual staining of live cells. The suite combines paired 3D time-lapse images acquired with and without fluorescent labels, a set of baseline models, and three metric tiers measuring pixel-level fidelity, organelle segmentation performance, and single-cell phenotype similarity. Using this evaluation suite, we study metric and model behavior across 3 cell types, 2 microscopes, 4 organelles, and 3 perturbation states. We find that regression baselines better predict the spatial localization of target organelles, whereas the generative baseline better captures the distribution of phenotypes across cells. These differences expose trade-offs between structural and phenotypic fidelity that are obscured by single-metric evaluation and suggest how virtual staining models can be developed for diverse downstream tasks such as localization, segmentation, tracking, and phenotypic profiling. We release the curated datasets, baseline checkpoints, and evaluation code as part of DynaCell, a broader framework for image-based profiling of cell-state dynamics.

title: A conditional generative model for T2-weighted prostate MRI with downstream evaluation in clinically significant cancer classificatio
desc: Scarce and unrepresentative training data limit the performance of prostate MRI prediction models. Synthetic T2-weighted (T2W) MRI may augment training data containing clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) and transition zone (TZ) lesions. In this retrospective, single-center, ethics-committee-approved study, we developed a conditional generative model for T2W prostate MRI extending MAISI-v2 with csPCa class, zonal, and lesion-mask-guided conditioning, incorporating a relative advantage weighted loss fine-tuned on 1,303 patients (1,654 lesions). Fidelity was assessed by incremental ablation, and downstream utility was evaluated with T2W-based csPCa classifiers across five simulated training-data scenarios, each testing 18 synthetic-data configurations. The proposed model reduced Fréchet inception distance (FID) from 13.28 (pretrained MAISI-v2) to $2.04 \pm 0.06$ internally (PI-CAI: $3.83 \pm 0.51$). Synthetic augmentation significantly increased AUC in all five scenarios (+0.027 to +0.088; adjusted $p = 0.016$--$0.043$), though cross-institutional augmentation of PI-CAI yielded a non-significant gain (+0.013; $p = 0.397$). Overall, our model improved T2W MRI fidelity, and synthetic images improved csPCa classification under simulated data constraints, although benefit did not transfer significantly across institutions.

title: Fuzzy-Enhanced Machine Learning Approach for Type 2 Diabetes Diagnosis
desc: Accurate diabetes prediction is critical for early clinical intervention, yet existing machine-learning pipelines often fail due to class imbalance, noisy physiological measurements, and redundant or weakly informative features. To address these unresolved limitations, this study establishes a unified fuzzy-evolutionary-ensemble framework designed to uncover a more discriminative feature space for type 2 diabetes prediction. The workflow integrates selective fuzzification of nonlinear clinical variables, SMOTE-ENN-based balancing and noise filtering, and Bat-Algorithm-driven evolutionary feature selection prior to training a Random Forest classifier. Applied to the Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset, the framework compresses the expanded fuzzy-numerical space into an optimized 10-feature subset and yields substantial performance gains: 96.11% accuracy, 95.14% precision, 98.00% recall, and a 98.23% F1-score. Relative to a baseline Random Forest using all 16 features (74.45% accuracy; 59.86% F1), the system achieves more than a 1.6-fold improvement in F1-score while preserving over 99% stability in majority-class detection and surpassing earlier published 16-feature models impacted by imbalance and weak feature relevance. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the integrated pipeline produces an enhanced fuzzy-numerical representation space that improves diabetes risk stratification and provides a scalable, uncertainty-aware foundation for diagnostic modeling across broader clinical datasets.

title: ECGJev: Question-Conditioned Option Scoring for 12-Lead ECG Interpretation
desc: Clinical interpretation of a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) often requires answering targeted diagnostic questions with clear, quantifiable decisions. We introduce ECGJev, the first ECG framework built on a decision decoder, a pretrained language model trained to return a probability for every listed option. A question-conditioned bridge compresses frozen waveform and spectrogram features into 16 ECG tokens, and a two-stage procedure adapts the bridge and low-rank adapters on the decoder's native option readout using diagnostic labels alone, scoring all options for a question in one forward pass. Evaluated across four ECG benchmarks, ECGJev achieves the highest macro-F1 on CPSC2018 (80.46%), PTB-XL (71.68%) and Chapman (96.86%), and generalizes competitively to the small-sample PTB cohort. Concept probes and perturbation analyses further show that its predictions rely directly on the ECG input, remain stable under option-order and wording variations, and transfer zero-shot to unseen waveform concepts. Our code is available at https://github.com/zhuoyuanli-lab/ECGJev.

title: Vision-language classification of Torsades de Pointes risk from pseudo-coloured ECG images: do T-wave morphology and colour context help or hinder?
desc: Contextual prompting is widely presented as a cheap route to better performance from vision models, but the evidence comes largely from benchmarks in which an attribute named in a prompt is also present in the image, confounding the two channels. We investigate the significance of context for a semantically complex biomedical signal classification task using a domain-adapted vision-language model, BiomedCLIP. Building on our previous work that renders electrocardiogram (ECG) signals as colour-enhanced images to flag Torsades de Pointes risk using the QT-nomogram and pseudo-colouring technique, we cross four context strategies with four T-wave morphology label sets, evaluated zero-shot and with a class-balanced linear probe, under five-fold stratified cross-validation on 9,789 images. Zero-shot inference is unusable. Once trained, the colour-enhanced images outperform the colourless ones on every metric: balanced accuracy 0.903 versus 0.825, sensitivity 0.914 versus 0.827, specificity 0.892 versus 0.823, ROC-AUC 0.955 versus 0.888 and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) 0.437 versus 0.311. Crossing colour-in-image with colour-in-prompt separates the confounded channels: the image contributes +0.126 MCC (+0.078 balanced accuracy, +0.067 ROC-AUC) whether or not the prompt names colour, whereas naming it changes nothing under any metric. Context is two-sided: the best prompt set gains 0.008 MCC where colour is present and 0.016 where it is not, while the worst loses 0.017 and 0.013. For a signal rendered as an image, the leverage lies in how the signal is drawn rather than in how it is described - and where the endpoint is an interval measurement, prompts naming T-wave morphology describe the wrong quantity.

title: Privacy-Preserving ECG-HRV Emotion Classification for Mood Swing Detection using Federated Learning on Constrained Edge Devices
desc: This paper presents a privacy-preserving mood monitoring framework that classifies emotional states from ECG-derived heart rate variability (HRV) features. The framework is evaluated on three public datasets comprising 74 participants and further validated using a wearable device in a pilot study. Leave-One-Participant-Out cross-validation (LOPO-CV) is used to assess generalization to unseen individuals. A series of experiments investigates the impact of temporal windowing, HRV feature selection, and class balancing on both four-class valence-arousal and binary valence classification. Results show that class balancing substantially improves minority-class recall, while Logistic Regression consistently outperforms five alternative classifiers and achieves competitive performance against HRV-based baselines. Pilot validation using a Polar H10 wearable achieves 75% binary valence accuracy on an unseen individual without calibration, demonstrating the feasibility of real-world deployment. To preserve privacy, the framework is also implemented using federated learning on a six-node Raspberry Pi cluster. Federated Logistic Regression achieves performance comparable to centralized training without sharing raw physiological data. These results demonstrate the potential of interpretable and privacy-preserving mood monitoring for continuous mental health assessment in clinical and community settings.

title: MedNet and U$^2$-ViT: A Nested Vision Transformer Diffusion Framework for Diverse Medical Images Generation
desc: The scarcity of diverse, high-quality medical images remains a significant bottleneck in advancing AI-driven medical diagnostics and treatment planning. Traditional datasets often suffer from class imbalances, limited disease coverage, and insufficient variations in imaging conditions - challenges that hinder the development of robust, generalizable models. To address this, we introduce MedNet, a large-scale, multi-modal text-to-image dataset spanning 61 disease categories with 160 classes, covering both humans and animals. We built this with images from trusted public repositories, ensuring data diversity, quality, and ethical compliance. Additionally, we propose U$^2$-ViT, a novel diffusion-based text-to-image generation architecture arranging Vision Transformers (ViTs) in a nested U-Net structure to enhance the generation of diverse, and high-fidelity medical images. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our model achieves the best Fr'echet Inception Distance (FID) score compared to state-of-the-art models. The source code is available at https://github.com/LakshmikarPolamreddy/MedNet-U2-ViT.

title: CONFIRM: Governing Scientific Reporting for Trustworthy Agentic Neuroimaging
desc: Large language model (LLM) agents can autonomously run neuroimaging analyses from research questions to reported findings. Existing agentic systems use tools to check that code runs and reported values match its output, but rely on LLM judgment to decide which results warrant scientific reporting. We show that LLM judges endorse site-confounded findings even when the confound is presented as evidence. We present \textbf{CONFIRM}, a framework that separates running an analysis from deciding which findings to report. CONFIRM encodes each hypothesis as a machine-readable, pre-specified analysis plan that fixes the claim and its pass criteria before computing results. It then filters results through five deterministic gates (search history and multiplicity, confounds, power, analytic stability, and replication) under three configurable reporting standards, from least to most demanding: \textit{Screen}, \textit{Replicate}, and \textit{Full}. Failed claims receive diagnoses that guide follow-up analyses. To evaluate reporting decisions at the claim level, we introduce \textbf{NeuroClaimBench}, comprising 489 executable neuroimaging claims with frozen data, including literature-supported findings and 150 controls designed to violate individual methodological requirements. On NeuroClaimBench, CONFIRM falsely supports at most 3\% of controls, compared with 23--38\% for the baselines, while recovering up to 61\% of literature-supported claims. When auditing an existing agent, CONFIRM reduces false support on controls from 23\% to 0\% while retaining the agent's literature-supported claims. Its diagnostic feedback also produces more supported revisions than Self-Refine with fewer LLM calls. Together, CONFIRM and NeuroClaimBench show that basing reporting decisions on pre-specified analysis plans and deterministic gates is essential for trustworthy autonomous scientific discovery.

title: OntoDoc: Automatically Generating Ontology Resource Descriptions
desc: Knowledge graphs and ontologies form the backbone of structured, machine-readable knowledge representation, yet ontology terms often lack natural language descriptions, limiting their accessibility and reuse. Existing ontology verbalization approaches tend to rely on rule-based or template-driven techniques that operate on strict, formal schema axioms, resulting in rigid verbalizations that fail to convey richer contextual semantics. We present OntoDoc, a multi-agent framework for automatically generating natural language descriptions for any Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI) within a SPARQL endpoint or RDF file. OntoDoc operates through a four-stage pipeline: (1) a Database Context agent that adaptively explores the knowledge graph via SPARQL to collect semantically informative triples about the target IRI; (2) a Web Context agent that retrieves and re-ranks encyclopedic background knowledge from Wikipedia and the open web; (3) an Assumption Generation agent that synthesizes both contexts into a structured, evidence-grounded list of intermediate assumptions; and (4) a Description Generation agent that produces the final natural language description from the grounded assumptions. We evaluate OntoDoc on three knowledge graphs spanning biomedical, agricultural, and cross-domain settings, using both automatic scoring via Large Language Models (LLMs) and human evaluation with 11 annotators. OntoDoc consistently matches or exceeds a naive LLM baseline and a template-based ontology verbalizer in accuracy. Furthermore, it vastly outperforms both baselines in the completeness of the generated descriptions, delivering an average 12% improvement in completeness over the naive baseline across all domains, and improving completeness scores by as much as 2.8 points on a 5-point scale relative to the ontology verbalizer.

title: Capacity Planning for Resource-Constrained Clinical LLM Serving
desc: Deploying large language models (LLMs) under a fixed accelerator budget requires jointly deciding how computational capacity is allocated across model sizes and how incoming requests are routed across that capacity. Although prior work has extensively studied LLM routing and serving efficiency, the relative importance of fleet composition and routing under resource constraints remains less understood. We investigate this question using a controlled four-GPU serving environment with heterogeneous clinical NLP workloads spanning short factual verification, biomedical semantic matching, and long-context clinical summarization. We systematically vary fleet composition, routing policy, and offered load while holding the workload trace and hardware budget fixed. Across 24 configurations, descriptive main-effect shares attribute more variation to fleet composition than to the evaluated routing policies in time to first token, latency, and long-context coverage. All-small fleets provide the best responsiveness and throughput but substantially lower long-context coverage, whereas larger-model capacity improves coverage at the cost of serving efficiency. Heterogeneous fleets provide intermediate operating points but can introduce strong-model bottlenecks when large-model capacity is scarce. In a focused evaluation of this bottleneck, capacity-aware routing reduces mean latency and increases throughput while incurring a small reduction in long-context coverage. Within this measured regime, the results support prioritizing capacity allocation, with routing managing demand within the provisioned capacity.

title: CheXPoT: Post-Hoc Visual Verification and Correction of VLM-Generated Radiology Reports
desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promise for chest radiograph report generation, but adoption remains limited because of hallucinated findings that are not grounded in the image. Correcting these hallucinations and improving overall report quality remains a significant challenge. Prior work has addressed this problem by refining models with reinforcement learning, preference optimization, or chain-of-thought supervision, often at substantial compute cost. To address this gap, we introduce CheXPoT, a program-of-thought (PoT) framework that verifies each generated finding against image features and removes those it cannot ground. CheXPoT decomposes generated reports into predicates with RadGraph and an LLM, grounds these predicates against a DenseNet-121 and Grad-CAM visual evidence table, executes PoT verification code, and rewrites reports after removing unsupported predicates. On a 4,145-image held-out split, CheXPoT yields statistically significant precision gains on 8 of 14 CheXpert classes and F1 gains on 5, with no significant decreases in either metric. CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 19.2% (MedGemma-4B) to 46.8% (MedGemma-4B + CheXPoT) and micro-average F1 from 23.0% to 49.4%, absolute gains of 27.6% and 26.4% respectively. We also tested CheXPoT on other VLM report generators. On LLaVA-Med, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 4.5% to 17.7% and micro-average F1 from 6.3% to 19.4%. On MAIRA-2, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 15.6% to 42.1% and micro-average F1 from 21.0% to 45.3%. Our results suggest that inexpensive post-hoc visual verification may improve VLM trustworthiness by correcting unsupported findings from generated reports. CheXPoT lays a foundation for tools that help validate VLM-generated radiology reports and reduce unsupported findings. These innovations may subsequently help increase trust and adoption of VLM tools in Medicine.

title: Quantifying Local and Global Fidelity of Nonlinear Embeddings
desc: Dimension reduction methods are chosen by a common claim: t-SNE and UMAP preserve local structure, and PCA preserves global structure. Checking it on given data takes local and global scores on one scale and a test that compares two maps. Both scores come from one curve. The locality profile is the chance-corrected share of each point's k nearest neighbors that a map keeps, over all neighborhood sizes. Its value at k = 10 is the local fidelity L, and its mean over 30 to 50 percent of the data is the global fidelity G. We prove that at the midpoint the profile is the agreement on which half of the data is near each point, a rank correlation of the distances. Because L and G are one statistic, two maps can be tested against each other. The LG reversal test applies to any two dimension reduction methods. It decides, with a block-jackknife p-value, whether one map is more local and the other more global, and returns the scale at which to change maps. On 156 maps of twelve datasets with up to 1.38 million points, G agrees with established global scores at 0.89 and 0.96, and 2,000 points estimate it. The test confirms the usual claim on seven datasets. On both retail datasets and both rolled-up manifolds, it finds the neighbor embeddings more global. In an agent memory of one million passages, the two maps cross at 150,000 passages (p = 2.6e-5). Applications span pathology, single cells, supply chains and AI agent memory.

title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR Metadata-First Infrastructure for AI-Enabled Science
desc: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. Moreover, the flow of value remains largely unidirectional: data move from collectors, through repositories and aggregators into models, and finally to research products or management actions. The derived value, such as corrected taxonomies, annotations, quality flags, and insights, rarely returns to source communities. We propose an extension of the original FAIR principles to address the needs of AI-ready infrastructure: the AI-FAIR metadata criteria, which place AI-enabled science in the context of a bidirectional Question-Data-Model triangle. This framework is designed to facilitate large-scale content-based analysis across diverse collections and ensure that the scientists generating the data benefit from the AI-enabled advances built on their data. Alongside these criteria, we introduce an agentic evaluation workflow that both rates existing datasets on the AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and provides actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. This modular dataset evaluation tool, paired with a domain-appropriate checklist, translates these principles into a reusable assessment of machine-learning readiness, AI-readiness for specified tasks, traceability, and ethical and CARE-aligned stewardship. Through this approach we aim to create a community-informed system to close the model data loop, so that AI also enriches data to further enable scientific discovery.

title: Poisson Super Learning For Survival And Competing Risks On A Discretized Time Scale
desc: We introduce the Poisson Super Learner, a scalable ensemble method for survival and competing risks prediction with right-censored data. The approach exploits the correspondence between the likelihood of piecewise-constant hazard models and the Poisson likelihood. After expanding the data over a chosen time partition, candidate hazard learners are trained under a common Poisson loss, and cross-validated log-hazard predictions are combined by a Poisson meta learner. The resulting ensemble is a geometric combination of candidate hazards, and can be used to estimate survival probabilities and cause-specific absolute risks. The Poisson Super Learner framework is modular and can in principle incorporate any learner that can estimate interval-specific hazards, including parametric, penalised, additive, and other machine-learning hazard models. Training targets the cause-specific hazard directly and does not require explicit modelling of the censoring distribution. For competing risks, separate cause-specific ensembles are fitted and subsequently combined to obtain individualised cumulative incidence predictions. We illustrate the approach using data from the Steno Diabetes Center collected between 2005 and 2022 to predict cardiovascular disease risk in patients with type 1 diabetes from detailed covariate information. The applied analysis is complemented by simulation studies designed to reflect key features of the data and to examine the behaviour of the method under controlled settings. All analyses were implemented using the freely available R software package poissonsuperlearner.

title: SurgPace: Complexity-Aware Progressive Distillation for Surgical Multimodal Large Language Models
desc: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

title: Bayesian Sequential Optimal Experimental Design for Single-Pixel Imaging using Reinforcement Learning
desc: Adaptive compressed sensing (CS) aims to select the most informative measurements sequentially, which is crucial for many modern imaging systems. This task can be formulated as a Bayesian sequential optimal experimental design (sOED) problem, where each new acquisition is chosen to maximally reduce uncertainty about the unknown image given prior information and subsequent data provided by acquisitions. However, in single-pixel imaging (SPI), the large design space consists of all possible binary illumination patterns. Directly optimizing the Bayesian sOED objective over this space using conventional methods is generally challenging. In this work, we reformulate sOED for SPI as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem. In RL, an agent learns a policy through repeated experimental trials to maximize a reward, here given as the expected information gain, the most complete measure of uncertainty reduction in Bayesian OED. This avoids the need to directly optimize complex information-theoretic objectives during a measurement to obtain the next design. Instead, the result is a learned policy function that directly maps the current posterior belief about the image to the next optimal binary measurement pattern, in a computationally efficient way. Using a simple yet representative SPI imaging scenario, this work evaluates the scalability of the learned policy under two different policy parameterizations. Furthermore, we investigate how performance deteriorates when only approximate posterior information is available or the measurements are impaired by noise, and propose several strategies to introduce additional design constraints motivated by biomedical applications.
